selection_snapshot.reason: Selected the highest-ranked feasible candidate for optimization goal 'balanced'.

proposal.rationale: The previous baseline at 640 exceeds the maximum latency constraint of 12.0 ms with 16.429 ms. Lowering the image size to 480 should reduce computational overhead and latency towards the target threshold while maintaining acceptable map50_95 performance above the 0.2 minimum.

The previous evaluation at 480 pixels successfully met the latency constraint of <12.0 ms (10.934 ms) and map50_95 constraint of >0.2 (0.236). To further reduce latency towards the balanced optimization goal while remaining above the accuracy threshold, testing the next lower available resolution of 416 pixels is warranted.

The resolution 448 is available and unmeasured, lying between 416 (latency 8.75ms, map50_95 0.207) and 480 (latency 10.93ms, map50_95 0.236). Testing 448 aims to find a configuration that meets the maximum latency constraint of 12.0ms while improving mAP above the 0.2 minimum threshold more reliably than 416.

The baseline image size of 640 yields a latency of 16.429 ms, which violates the maximum latency constraint of 12.0 ms while exceeding the mAP requirement. To reduce latency and meet the constraint, we should explore the smallest available image size, 416, which is expected to significantly lower inference time on CPU.

The latency at 640 (16.4ms) violates the 12ms constraint, while 416 meets latency (8.75ms) and map50_95 (0.207 > 0.2). Testing 448 explores the resolution space between 416 and 640 to find the highest resolution that satisfies the maximum median latency constraint of 12.0 ms while potentially improving accuracy over 416.

The previous evaluation at 448 achieved a map50_95 of 0.222 with a median latency of 10.628 ms, staying well under the 12.0 ms constraint. Since 480 is the next available image size, testing it will help determine if we can gain accuracy while keeping the latency below the maximum limit.

The baseline at size 640 exceeds the latency constraint of 12.0ms with 16.429ms while comfortably exceeding the map50_95 requirement. Reducing the image size to 512 is expected to decrease inference latency toward the target limit while retaining sufficient accuracy margin above the minimum map50_95 of 0.2.

Tested sizes 640 and 512 exceeded the latency constraint of 12.0 ms or the 512 size achieved 11.279 ms. To safely reduce latency further while staying close to the validated 512 resolution and exploring the available sizes, 480 is the next logical untested candidate to approach the target latency envelope.

Measured evidence shows that 512 achieves 11.279ms latency (under the 12.0ms limit) with a mAP of 0.243 (above the 0.2 minimum). While 640 exceeds latency limits, testing 576 from the available sizes will help find the optimal resolution closer to the latency ceiling to maximize accuracy while remaining valid.

limitations: Live LLM choices reveal archived measurements, not new benchmarks.
Initial 640 was chosen after inspecting prior results; exploratory evaluation.
Historical measurements have differing software environments.
Repeated LLM calls may be identical and are not necessarily independent.
Elapsed time covers proposal calls, not model evaluation.
Tokens, internal provider retries and monetary cost are not measured.
